title: Descent of a geometric cohomological dimension bound
statement:
Let $X$ be a finite-type
scheme over a field $K$, and let $\overline K$ be an algebraic
closure. If $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(K)\leq c$ and
$\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X_{\overline K})\leq e$, then
$\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X)\leq c+e$, using
[def-sc-etale-torsion-cd].

proof.text: Finite type over K makes X locally Noetherian and quasi-separated. Quasi-compactness of a over the compact affine base makes X quasi-compact. Fix torsion F and n>c+e. Apply the proved Etale.subsingleton_H_of_isTorsion, recorded in [lem-sc-torsion-bounded-exponent-vanishing], so it suffices to consider G killed by a positive integer N.

For q>e, [lem-sc-field-higher-direct-image-stalk] identifies the geometric stalk of R^q a_*G at Spec L with H^q(X_L,G|). Pullback preserves torsion, so the geometric dimension bound kills this group. The single point Spec L → Spec K is a surjective family because Spec K has one point. Mathlib conservative families of lifted etale points are jointly faithful on abelian sheaves. Transfer zero along uliftSheafFiberIso and apply joint faithfulness to id=0 to get R^q a_*G=0. No Galois-module equivalence is needed.

For every q, the additive ordinary right-derived functor sends N·id_G=0 to N·id_(R^q a_*G)=0, directly making each higher direct image torsion. The field bound gives H^p(Spec K,R^q a_*G)=0 for p>c. Apply the proved Leray rectangle bound [lem-sc-leray-vanishing-bound] to the row and column vanishings, obtaining H^n(X,G)=0 for n>c+e. Step 1 gives the same vanishing for F, exactly the stated cohomological dimension bound.
